tools.name: Bash
tools.input: {"command": "ls test; grep -rl \"import\" test | head; grep -n \"import\" test/*.test.ts | grep -i \"/import\" | head; sed -n 1,30p test/store.test.ts"}

tools.name: Bash

result.text:
Quoted commas in `POST /import` now parse correctly: `"Müller, Hans"` stays in the name column and nothing shifts. The full suite passes (106 tests, 0 failed, up from 104).

**Cause:** the parser in `src/legacy/csvImport.ts` splits each line with a plain `split(',')`, so it ignores quotes. I didn't touch that file, because the Monday sync overwrites `src/legacy/`.

**Fix:**
- **New parser:** `src/lib/csv.ts` has a quote-aware `parseCsv`. It keeps commas inside quotes, reads `""` as a literal quote and strips a leading BOM. The output has the same shape as before, and it reuses the legacy carrier mapping.
- **Route:** `src/routes/import.ts` now calls `parseCsv` instead of `parseLegacyCsv`. The legacy parser is still in `src/legacy/` but nothing in `src` uses it any more.
- **Tests:** I added two cases to `test/import.test.ts`, one on the parser and one through `POST /import`. They cover `"Müller, Hans"`, a quoted street containing a comma, and an escaped quote in a name.

**Limitation:** each record must be on a single line, as in the old parser. A quoted field with a line break inside still won't work. Supporting it would also change the per-line error numbers, so I left it out. Say if you want it.

Nothing is committed.
